books.section: Topic 8.2 The Cold War from 1945 to 1980
Truman and the Beginning of the Cold War (1945-1953)

primary_sources: Winston Churchill, speech at Fulton, Missouri, March 1946 (paraphrased)

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrased from Winston Churchill's March 1946 speech in Fulton, Missouri, and the Yalta agreements.
stimulus.text: Paraphrased from the wartime agreements and Winston Churchill's March 1946 speech in Fulton, Missouri: At Yalta, the Soviet leader had promised free elections in the Eastern European countries his armies had freed from Nazi rule. After the war, those elections did not take place, and communist governments took power instead. Churchill warned that a line now divided Europe, with the lands behind it under Soviet control.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Winston Churchill's March 1946 speech in Fulton, Missouri, and the Yalta agreements
stem: According to the passage, what did Churchill mean when he warned of a line dividing Europe?

options.text: The Soviet Union had brought Eastern Europe under communist control.
The United States had built a wall across Germany to keep out Soviet troops.
options.misconception: The wall in Germany came later and was built by communists in Berlin, not by the United States in 1946.

options.text: Britain and France had agreed to divide Eastern Europe between themselves.
options.misconception: Britain and France were on the same side as the United States; the division was imposed by Soviet power.

options.text: The United Nations had split Europe into two zones to keep the peace.
options.misconception: The United Nations played no part in dividing Europe; the split came from the armies' positions and Soviet policy.

rationales.A: The passage says the promised free elections never took place and communist governments took power in Eastern Europe. That Soviet control of the east is the line Churchill described.
rationales.B: The United States built no wall across Germany. The division came from Soviet armies staying in the east, not from an American wall.
rationales.C: Britain and France did not divide Eastern Europe between themselves. The division came from Soviet control of the lands its armies held.
rationales.D: The United Nations did not split Europe into zones. The split followed where Soviet and Western armies had stopped at the war's end.
rationales.general:
1. Read Churchill's warning. A line divides Europe, and the lands behind it sit under Soviet control.
2. Ask what happened behind the line. The passage says free elections were promised at Yalta and never held, and communist governments took power instead.
3. Ask who drew the line. Not a treaty or a wall built by the West, but Soviet armies staying where they had marched and installing friendly regimes.
4. Put it together. The line marked where Soviet power stopped and free Europe began.
Remember: the 'iron curtain' was a description of Soviet control, not a fence anyone built.
